subject: Request: no-auto-fallback impact assessment for Solace pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Oct 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: no-auto-fallback impact assessment for Solace pilot

Vanessa / team —

Quick ask: Solace Therapeutics (D-93472) confirmed that for their upcoming pilot we cannot allow automatic fallback to any alternate model variants or cross-region routing. Their auditors require deterministic serving: one model variant pinned to the us-east region for all inference and no transparent fallback.

Can infra/ops/product give a short impact assessment (capacity, latency SLO risk, monitoring gaps) and a runbook for the pilot timeline? Specifically we need:
- What changes are required to disable auto-fallback at the routing layer and pin to a single variant+region?
- Can we guarantee no-kick-to-other-variants under overload? If not, what degradation modes are possible?
- What is the effort & timeline to implement a canary (10% traffic) with rollback hooks?

I've attached the customer MOP and their security Q&A (two files). Customer timeline: start of pilot week-of 2025-11-03.

Thanks — please reply with owners and ETA.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: solace_no_fallback_mop_v1.pdf (pdf, 154KB), solace_security_q4_answers.docx (docx, 92KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Oct 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: no-auto-fallback impact assessment for Solace pilot

Thanks Marissa — a few clarifying Qs from infra side before we scope work:

1) "No automatic fallback" — do they mean no fallback at all (requests must fail if pinned capacity is saturated) or do they allow queued requests / degraded throughput on the same variant? That changes the answer a lot.
2) Which model family/size are they pinning? Large encoder-decoder models may need additional pool sizing. If they give us the exact model artifact name we can run a memory/runtime profile.
3) Is cross-AZ allowed within the same region? We can pin to us-east but still use AZ diversity for reliability if permitted.

Immediate notes:
- If they disallow fallback and also disallow queued throttling then the only safe mode is strict request rejection at SLO breach — which is straightforward but customer-visible failures.
- We can implement a canary route that pins 10% traffic to a reserved pool (dedicated capacity). That requires reserved capacity reservation and a short config change in the routing policy.

I can prototype a routing flag (no_fallback=true) and simulate in our staging cluster this week. If they supply the model name now we can estimate GPU-hours and policy changes.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
karthik@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Oct 2025 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: no-auto-fallback impact assessment for Solace pilot

Agree with Karthik. A couple product-level tradeoffs to call out:

- Canary + auto-rollback: We should offer a canary with automatic rollback triggers (error rate & latency thresholds). For Solace we need to confirm whether automatic rollback to a fallback variant is permitted as a mitigation after canary detects regressions — my read of the ask is no, but if we can get a conditional exception for rollback under an agreed audit trail that may reduce risk.
- Observability: we must surface token-level lineage (which variant served the response) and an immutable audit log for the pilot window. That will need retention tweaks in Console.
- SLA language: Sales/legal will need explicit language that if we honor no-fallback and capacity is exceeded, customer accepts potential 503 behavior. Legal may want an SLA carveout.

Irene — can security/legal confirm whether the Q&A answers we have cover the audit logging requirement?

I'd propose owners: Karthik (runtime changes + canary), Irene (security/legal), Marissa (customer coordination), Vanessa (commercial & escalation). ETA for a staging prototype: 7 business days assuming model artifact is provided.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Principal Product Manager, Serving
priyom@redwood.com

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@solacethera.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Oct 2025 08:06:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: no-auto-fallback impact assessment for Solace pilot

Marissa / Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. To be explicit: Solace cannot accept any invisible fallback to a different variant or region. Our compliance team requires deterministic logs and artifact hashes for every inference request; any automatic fallback would void our audit. We are OK with 503-style failures if their only cause is capacity saturation.

Model we will pin to: solace-qa-13b-v2 (public artifact id included in the MOP). We will also provide a short list of test prompts for pre-launch validation.

We can discuss conditional rollback but only if there is a signed addendum that we keep for audits.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of AI, Solace Therapeutics
sanjay.patel@solacethera.com

Subject: Re: Request: no-auto-fallback impact assessment for Solace pilot

Team — thanks for the assessments and Sanjay for confirming constraints. Summarizing next steps and owners so we have a single place of record: 

1) Karthik: prototype routing flag (no_fallback=true) + AZ behavior test and staging validation for model solace-qa-13b-v2. Deliverable: staging runbook & GPU sizing estimate. ETA: 2025-10-20 EOD.

2) Priyom: define canary plan (10% traffic), rollback triggers (latency > 2x baseline OR error rate > 1.5%), and the audit trail fields we need surfaced in Console. Deliverable: canary plan doc + observability checklist. ETA: 2025-10-21.

3) Irene / Legal: review Solace Q&A and provide language for the pilot contract clause (no-fallback SLA carveout, audit retention). Deliverable: redline to pilot agreement. ETA: 2025-10-22.

4) Marissa: coordinate with Solace on test prompts + sign-off on the addendum if we require conditional rollback. Deliverable: signed MOU/addendum or explicit written waiver. ETA: 2025-10-24.

Commercial note: we will provision a small dedicated pool for the pilot to avoid contention with hosted customers; finance to follow on capacity commit & pricing. Vanessa will own the commercial approval loop.

I'll create a short playbook entry under the Solace drive link and add the staging runbook once Karthik uploads it. If any owner cannot meet ETA, flag here with blockers.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts (Sales)
vanessa@redwood.com
